findings.reasoning: Appendix A4 reports the mean pooled animal score as 0.175 with s.e.m. 0.161 and 'maximum score of 1.34'. The metric throughout the paper is noise-corrected RSA Pearson's r, which is a correlation bounded on [-1, 1]. A maximum of 1.34 is mathematically impossible (probability/correlation > 1). This is further confirmed by the Fig. 4b caption, which reports the same quantity as 'the maximum between all pairs of animals is 0.34' and the mean as 0.18 (consistent with the 0.175 mean here). The '1.34' is almost certainly a typo for '0.34', but as printed it is a correction-worthy impossible value and an internal text-figure inconsistency.
contradiction_locations: Appendix A4 'maximum score of 1.34' exceeds correlation bound of 1.0
Fig. 4b caption reports the same maximum as 0.34

findings.reasoning: Fig. 4b caption: mean animal-to-animal score 0.18 and maximum 0.34. Both values are within the valid [0,1] correlation range and are consistent with the mean of 0.175 reported in Appendix A4. The 0.34 maximum is the correct value; only the Appendix A4 '1.34' is wrong.

The reported statistics (r = 0.59 linear trend, raw-input correlation 0.46, parameter counts 3.80e7 vs 6.38e7) are all within valid bounds and internally plausible. No mathematical contradiction can be established from the reported numbers alone.

Body text reports r = 0.59 while the embedded Fig. 5b legend text shows r = 0.60. This is a minor rounding discrepancy of the same best-fit correlation (0.59 vs 0.60), explicitly the class of 'minor rounding discrepancies' that should not be flagged as a critical statistical error.

The methods state neural responses 'are binned into intervals of approximately 45-50 ms, corresponding neatly with the 15-20 Hz whisking frequency typical of rodents (50 ms per cycle at 20 Hz)'. Numeric check: 1/45 ms = 22.2 Hz and 1/50 ms = 20 Hz, so a 45-50 ms bin corresponds to 20-22.2 Hz, not 15-20 Hz. A 15 Hz cycle would be 66.7 ms, well outside the 45-50 ms bin. Only the 50 ms / 20 Hz edge case is consistent. The claimed correspondence between the bin size and the lower end of the whisking-frequency range is numerically off by ~30%. (Note: 'five sub-timesteps (~9 ms each)' = 45 ms is internally consistent with the 45 ms bin.)
contradiction_locations: 45-50 ms bin corresponds to 20-22.2 Hz, not 15-20 Hz; 15 Hz would require 66.7 ms bins
